_source: Colors: Extron's Afterburn theme guide, transcribed in docs/design-rules.md section 4; `alert` from the seed's own record icon.
Type, borders, button archetypes and sizes: surveyed off seeds/Afterburn 1035.gdl (its fonts, border resources and every button's per-state fill, stroke and text color).
Point sizes draw at 1.375 px per point, GUI Designer's 99 DPI (gdl/compose.py PT).
A level: every Afterburn seed's Level (300M, 320, 525) is 15 px across, its fill gaugeFillColorField in accent-2 - Build draws a Level over its whole box, so the box is the rail.

Slider and level: the seed's built sliders (Audio Settings) - a 10 px rail (SliderTrackWidth) in a 50 x 395 control, the empty rail the control's fill (#242634, TLPMinValueImageID), the filled rail #BABCCE (TLPMaxValueImageID), a 50 px #626ACF thumb (SliderIndicatorImageID) - matching the guide's track, slider-fill and secondary-accent rows.
Panel: the seed's filled container - raised fill, #6A6E89 stroke, Afterburn - 10 Radius 2 Thick - and the guide's 'shapes #6A6E89' row.

Themes: the guide's four background images and Extron's recommended accent scheme for each (Default + 1, Anthracite + 3, Blue Slate + 2, Grape + 4; guide pp.8-9), from the resource kit's Backgrounds/6400x4000/TLP 1025 & 1220 files - the variant the seed's own 6400x4000_bg1.png was made from (its recorded filename and byte size match). The image is the raised card that elevates the page's main area, transparent around it so the page color shows.

Layout: the seed's own pages (Start, Main Select Source, Main VC, Main SD), rendered from their built artwork: every page puts its task in the background image's squircle and the same few controls in the rails either side.

Image buttons and the kit: every image button in the Afterburn 1035 and 1535 seeds - the kit file on each state (buttonImageField), drawn Fill and MiddleCenter, with no border resource; the fill, caption and indent each archetype uses; and the kit's own naming (Resources/Afterburn/Buttons/PNG: <size>_<icon>_nsel for unselected, <size>_<icon>-<accent>_sel per accent). Icon anatomy: the guide's p.4.

Slider thumb: the kit's 440x440_thumb-1 draws its circle across 286 of 440 px (65%), and the seed's built 50 px thumb shows a circle 31-32 px across - so the canvas draws the kit's own thumb, not a circle the size of the box.
title: Extron Afterburn
tagline: Extron's Afterburn touch-panel template, for TLP Pro panels.

colors.name: page
colors.usage: Page and popup background; a slider or level's empty track over an image, or on a raised panel.

colors.name: raised
colors.usage: Button fill when idle; panels and cards; a slider or level's empty track over a color.

colors.name: pressed
colors.usage: Button fill when pressed or selected (the On state). The same value as page.

colors.name: text
colors.usage: Headings, button captions, paragraphs; the border of a pressed outlined button. On page, raised and pressed.

colors.name: text-secondary
colors.usage: Subheadings, date and time, divider lines, the border of an idle outlined button, the filled part of a slider, single-color icons. On page and raised.

colors.name: text-subtle
colors.usage: Icon secondary in the guide: the de-emphasised parts of an icon. Under 4.5:1 on page and raised, so never for text people have to read.

colors.name: shape
colors.usage: Container shapes: the outline of a panel or card (over a raised fill, as the seed's own container draws it) and of the seed's round indicators; a toggle's thumb when off.

colors.name: accent
colors.usage: Selection lines and selected icons - the kit's `_sel` images draw both, in the scheme's accent - and the caption of a selected text-only button (a numbered preset, a search result), as the seed's are. Not a fill: Afterburn never fills a button with it. One scheme per project.

colors.name: accent-2
colors.usage: A slider's thumb and a level's fill (the guide's secondary accent). One scheme per project.

colors.name: alert
colors.usage: An alert: a red fill with a white caption, for a condition someone has to act on - a fault, a warning. Not for an ordinary action such as shutting down. Never a caption color - Afterburn shows state with icons in the accent colors, not with colored text. The red is the seed's own record icon's.

colors.name: scrim
colors.usage: What the panel shows behind a modal popup's card: the page beneath, under black at 65% (alpha 166). Build draws it over every modal whatever background it was given - measured on the Afterburn, Mach and Shockwave seeds and on a panel built from a canvas - so it is not one of a panel's six colors. The guide's #242634 at 20% transparency is not what ships.

type.name: title
type.usage: A page's title - the seed's largest label.

type.name: heading
type.usage: A popup's or a section's heading.

type.name: button-large
type.usage: The caption of a large button: a source, a main action.

type.name: body
type.usage: Labels, status and paragraphs; the clock.

type.name: body-strong
type.usage: A label that names a group of controls.

type.name: button
type.usage: The caption of a small button. Afterburn's own small buttons use 13 pt, under the 14 pt minimum the toolkit checks, so 14 is the floor here.

afterburn.usage: An outlined button: rounded, with its stroke drawn.

afterburn-flat.usage: A rounded fill with no stroke: ghost buttons, panels, cards.

rect.usage: A square-cornered fill: a full-width bar.

afterburn-ellipse.usage: An icon button's pressed fill: a circle behind the icon (guide Fig. 7).

none.usage: No border at all: a kit image button, whose image draws the whole button.

outlined.usage: The default button: a raised fill and a text-secondary border, pressed fill and a white border when On. The seed's most common look. With an `icon` the icon sits at its left and the caption after it (Swap, Contacts, End Call); with an icon and no caption, the icon is centered (a keyboard key).

ghost.usage: No fill until pressed or selected: list rows, tabs, icon buttons.

inverse.usage: For a button sitting on a raised panel: pressed fill when idle, raised when On.

source.usage: A horizontal list button: a large icon with its label under it, for choosing a source or a camera. Selected, it takes the pressed fill and the kit draws the icon in the accent with an accent line along the bottom. The seed's are 110x110 in a row.
source.caption: below

list.usage: A vertical list button: an icon, then its label, for a set of options down the left rail (Display, Lighting, Make Call). Selected, it takes the raised fill and the kit draws the icon in the accent with an accent line down the left. The seed's are 178x50.
list.caption: indent

icon.usage: An icon button: the icon alone, no outline, for a stand-alone control (Help, Power, Close, mute under the volume slider). Pressed, a round fill behind it, and the icon in the accent where the kit has a selected one. The seed's are 64x64.
icon.caption: none

toggle.usage: A toggle: its label at the left and the switch at the right, for turning one thing on or off (a display's power, a mute). The thumb moves and takes the secondary accent when On. The seed's are 178x50.
toggle.caption: indent

alert.usage: An alert: a red fill and a white caption, for a condition someone has to act on - a fault, a warning, an alarm. Not for an ordinary action, even a final one like shutting the room down: a confirmation is an outlined button. A designer can still choose red where they want it.

kit.note: Extron's Afterburn resource kit. Each icon comes unselected (`off`) and selected in each accent's color; a family drawn in the primary accents (orange, light-blue, gold, med-blue) selects in the scheme's primary, one drawn in the secondary accents (periwinkle, light-green, gold) - toggles, volume levels - in its secondary.

cover.pattern: rounded tiles cut at the Afterburn 10 px radius

iconography.icon_prop: The kit draws each icon unselected and selected in every accent, with the selection line where the variant has one, so the button's states show themselves: state 0 unselected, the rest selected in the page's accent.
iconography.intro: Afterburn shows state with icons, not with colored text. Every icon comes from Afterburn's own resource kit through a Button's `icon` - never draw one, and never color a caption red.
rules: **Anatomy** (the guide's p.4): a `text-secondary` (#BABCCE) stroke and primary elements, `text-subtle` (#767789) secondary elements, an `icon-ground` (#414459) background inside the icon, and - selected - the supporting element in the accent. The kit already draws all of this, for every accent scheme.

**Which button**: a stand-alone control (help, power, close, mute) is `variant="icon"`, 64x64. Sources and cameras are `source`, a row of squares with the label under the icon. Options down the left rail are `list`, a selection line at the left when chosen. On and off is `toggle`. An important action with a label is `outlined` with an `icon` (End Call, Swap).

**Feedback**: state 0 draws the icon unselected, the others selected - in the accent, with the variant's selection line and fill. A single-image icon (`power`, `call_connected`) still shows it is pressed.

**Alerts** are `variant="alert"`: a red fill with a white caption, for a condition someone has to act on - a fault, a warning - and one per screen at most. An ordinary action, even a final one like shutting the room down, is an outlined button unless the designer asks for red.

examples.states_note: In Afterburn a state shows itself with its icon: the kit's selected image draws the icon in the accent, with the selection line for a list button, and the button takes the pressed fill. A text-only button that is selected shows its caption in `accent`. Never color a caption red.
examples.group_note: Both defaults are Afterburn's own source row: four 110x110 buttons, 49 px apart.
examples.color_rule: `page` behind everything; `raised` for idle buttons and panels, with `shape` outlining a card; `pressed` and a `text` border for On; `text` and `text-secondary` for type; `accent` only through the kit's selected icons and selection lines, and the caption of a selected text-only button; `alert` only as an alert's fill, with a `text` caption; `accent-2` is the slider thumb, a level's fill and a toggle's thumb.

themes.name: Default
themes.usage: The Default background with accent scheme 1: Extron's recommended pairing, and the seed's own.

themes.name: Anthracite
themes.usage: The Anthracite background with accent scheme 3, as Extron recommends.

themes.name: Blue Slate
themes.usage: The Blue Slate background with accent scheme 2, as Extron recommends.

themes.name: Grape
themes.usage: The Grape background with accent scheme 4, as Extron recommends.

layout.main_note: The central squircle: the raised card the background image draws, 183-1099 across and 24-776 down on a 1280x800 page (the image's opaque body, measured).
regions: **The squircle holds the page's main task.** A centered title (`title` for a room name on the start page, `subheading` for a section), the sources or the selected device's controls in the middle, and one outlined action centered at its foot (Preview, Press to begin). The date sits bottom-left inside it and the time bottom-right, in `text-secondary` - or both together, bottom-center, on the start page.

**The left rail (x 0-183) holds grouped secondary controls:** a `body` heading per group (Display, Settings, Lights, VTC) at x 14, and under it a column of list buttons - ghost, left-aligned, about 160x58 - or toggles. Its foot holds the one outlined button that switches mode (Presentation, Video Conference), about 144x64 at 20,706.

**The right rail (x 1099-1280) holds volume and the system controls:** a `Volume` heading, the vertical slider (Afterburn draws it 50x395 at 1168,202; make it 54 wide at 1166, since 50 is under the 53 px touch minimum the toolkit checks) with mute under it, an outlined action at the top (Start Sharing, 144x64 at 1121,30), and help and power at the foot.
Nothing else goes outside the squircle. A full-page grid of controls is a working panel but not an Afterburn one.

_source: Series, sizes, DPI and tier: GUI Designer's own TemplateInfoTable.config, through gdl/templates.py; each series' models are the MODELS_FULL models gdl.templates.template_for gives it (by model, never by resolution alone: Afterburn has no 720 template, so no TLP720T row).

main: the opaque body (alpha 255) of the series' main-page background art, mapped onto the canvas the way the template's page draws it (fit: Fill or Stretch). No control draws the squircle; the image does. The 1220's is the profile's own earlier measurement (183, not 182 - both end at 1099).
rail: what the canvas leaves beside the main region - right of it on every series that has room, below it (a footer, running across) on the 320 and the portrait 300.
popup: the template's standard popup region, where it fills a quarter of the canvas or more.

backgrounds: the kit's four page backgrounds per size, for the main page (the 520 and 535 split theirs into _start and _main; a working page takes _main). image is the name the template gives its default; the others take the kit file's name. The 1720 draws the 1520's 6830x3840 art, as its template does.

seeds, kinds, borders: each seed in seeds/ by part number and canvas (both 300M seeds are one part, either way up), and one of a model's other way up where no template is drawn so - a turned seed - under its panel (TLP1035M-Portrait) - what control kinds it can clone (the 525, 320 and 300M seeds have levels and no slider; the 320 has no standard popup), and each profile border it lacks mapped to its own of the same thickness and nearest radius.

frame: the series' working page in its template's own grammar, off its own seed (tests/measure_series.py frame_of; --frame prints each); its keys are docs/claude-design.md section 2's *Frame*. Afterburn's working page is Main SD, with no top or bottom bar: its art draws the centre (main), the source tabs across the centre's top, and the columns either side are the rails. The 520's is its Main, a hub; the 320's its Doc Cam 1 and the 300s' their Computer, each standing around its own page's art.
